theorem continuousAt_def' : ContinuousAt f x ↔ Tendsto f (𝓝 x) (𝓝 (f x)) :=
  Iff.rfl

This is a piece of #36769 that we found useful, I'm actually very suprised this never existed before and the current docs#continuousAt_def is not hot continuousAt is defined! Should we (open another separate PR) and add this lemma?
cc @Jiang Jiedong @Yakov Pechersky

I think that there is no doubt people do use this direct definition of ContinuousAt frequently. But there is no way to use it unless one do defeq abuse or unfolding the definition.

Currently in mathlib, there exist many tactics just unfolding the definition of ContinuousAt. Searching for simp \[[^\]]*ContinuousAt(?!\.)[^\]]*\] returns 7 results and searching for rw \[[^\]]*ContinuousAt(?!\.)[^\]]*\] returns 51 results. Searching for unfold ContinuousAt also returns 1 result.
There could be more defeq abuse that I don't know how to find out.

So the problem is more about the general principle. Should we avoid unfolding the definitions directly and add def lemmas or should we allow people to write unfolding tactics.

I would support the first one: avoid unfolding the definitions. If this is an intended usage of the definition, its APIs should be provided explicitly.
My argument is that: there are cases that by design, one should not unfold the definition (like using Classical.choose in the definition). This principle will help us to detect and prevent someone doing something breaks the design.
#31745
If you really think people shouldn't unfold ContinuousAt you could @[unexpose] it, but I expect people to be opposed since the defeq is nice.
Emm... I think in this specific case, the definition of continuousAt is not so "canonical". We have a theorem called continuousAt_def that have this _def name but with a different statement....
we also have ContinuousAt.tendsto that converts one way the definition, but no ContinuousAt.of_tendsto
I think the definition of ContinuousAt is quite canonical. Anyway, Edison's suggested lemma is functionally the same as ContinuousAt.eq_def and most likely doesn't need adding
It's autogenerated?

The advantage of a manual lemma over eq_def is that it can remain the same if the definition changes, while eq_def must change with it. I'd personally be in favour of adding a lemma (though perhaps not with a prime in the name), but I don't think there's consensus on having them
Yes, and my point is that the definition is canonical enough that it won't change again
I appreciate that, but the future is long and unpredictable :)

Yaël Dillies said:

I think the definition of ContinuousAt is quite canonical. Anyway, Edison's suggested lemma is functionally the same as ContinuousAt.eq_def and most likely doesn't need adding

My point is first ContinuousAt.eq_def is not a good name for definitional lemmas (also it's still unfolding the definition), secondly using x_def instead of plain unfolding makes refactor of definition a lot easier (we only need to reprove that lemma), thirdly (very specific to this instance), continuousAt_def doesn't say what we expect it to say!
Well, maybe ContinuousAt was defined as the RHS of docs#continuousAt_def at some point, and someone refactored the definition and enjoyed the "need to only reprove the lemma" :woman_shrugging:

Let me put it another way: _def lemmas are useless because either we don't update them when we change the definition and they diverge from it (unexpected, as you say), or we do at which point we might as well have used the auto-generated .eq_def lemma.

IMO .eq_def works completely different than having a def lemma, .eq_def = unfolding and using x_def means rewriting, I don't think they are the same thing at all and if your point is we should just be unfolding definitions then what makes it better than having a harmless x_def lemma?

We can always make the name better, a lemma called continuousAt_def may still suffer from definition changing, but we could rename it to continuousAt_iff_tendsto to make it more stable across definition changes.
I also suggest to change the name of current continuousAt_def lemma, because it is simply not accurate. What about continuousAt_iff_preimage_mem_nhds?

The complicating issue here is that the current def lemma is also implicitly unfolding the definition of Tendsto. That's why it can be proven with Iff.rfl currently. And Tendsto is I think canonically going to be the preimage mem nhds form.

Yakov Pechersky said:

The complicating issue here is that the current def lemma is also implicitly unfolding the definition of Tendsto. That's why it can be proven with Iff.rfl currently.

Double defeq abuse :/
I think some would call it defeq use :)
At your call site, what about the precise Tendsto syntactic form do you need? For a targeted rewrite?
Yes, a precise Tendsto is needed for rewrite.
rw [continuousAt_def', map_zero, WithZeroTopology.tendsto_zero]
can we also have an unfolding lemma for Tendsto?
